label: The Universal Phase Space
notes: Open by promising the first big family of symplectic manifolds. Every smooth manifold X spawns a cotangent bundle that already carries a canonical symplectic form, no extra choices required. Stress that this is the geometric home of classical mechanics: positions live on X, momenta in the fibers.

label: Cotangent Coordinates
notes: Explain how a chart on X induces a chart on the cotangent bundle. The base coordinates are positions and the fiber coefficients are the components of a covector in the dual basis of differentials. Warn that fiber coefficients transform by the inverse-transpose Jacobian, unlike tangent vectors.

label: The Tautological One-Form
notes: This is the heart of the lecture. A point of the cotangent bundle is itself a covector sitting over a base point. The tautological form feeds a tangent vector upstairs through the projection's differential, then lets that resident covector evaluate it. Emphasize that no auxiliary data enters the definition.

label: Alpha in Coordinates
notes: Show that the intrinsic recipe collapses to the clean formula sum of p dq once a chart is chosen. Walk through why the projection kills the vertical part and why only the base differentials survive. The formula is a coordinate shadow, not a coordinate accident.

label: Coordinate Independence
notes: Demonstrate that alpha is well defined by changing charts on the base. The base map and the inverse-transpose fiber rule conspire so that the new sum of p dq equals the old one. Mention the notebook's symbolic pullback check, where the coefficient simplifies exactly back to xi.

label: The Canonical Symplectic Form
notes: Define omega as minus the exterior derivative of alpha. Because omega is exact it is automatically closed, so half the symplectic axiom comes for free. In coordinates omega becomes the standard sum of dq wedge dp, the model two-form from the previous lecture.

label: Nondegeneracy and Volume
notes: Confirm the second axiom: the coordinate matrix of omega is the standard block form with nonzero determinant, so omega is nondegenerate. Its top exterior power omega to the n is a nowhere-vanishing volume form, orienting the manifold. Reference the notebook determinant ledger across dimensions.

label: Naturality of the Lift
notes: State the functoriality theorem. Any diffeomorphism of the base lifts canonically to the cotangent bundle by pushing covectors with the inverse-transpose differential. This cotangent lift pulls the tautological form back to itself, hence pulls omega back to omega, so it is a symplectomorphism.

label: The Cylinder Example
notes: Make naturality concrete on the cotangent bundle of the circle, a cylinder. A circle diffeomorphism bends the coordinate grid, but the lifted fiber coordinate divides by the derivative so the area coefficient of dtheta wedge dxi stays one. This is the notebook's exact pullback computation in picture form.

label: A Symplectomorphism Caveat
notes: Sharpen the theorem with a non-example. Translating each fiber vertically preserves omega yet does not come from any base diffeomorphism. So cotangent lifts inject into symplectomorphisms but do not surject. This separates the natural family from the full symmetry group.

label: Lagrangian Submanifolds
notes: Introduce the two distinguished half-dimensional submanifolds. The zero section, covectors equal to zero, and each cotangent fiber over a fixed base point both make alpha and hence omega vanish on them. They are the first Lagrangian submanifolds, a theme that will recur throughout the course.

label: Recap and Outlook
notes: Summarize the construction chain: intrinsic alpha, canonical omega equals minus d alpha, automatic closedness, coordinate nondegeneracy, and naturality under lifts. Preview that these cotangent models seed Lagrangian and tubular-neighborhood theorems later, and assign the volume and homework exploration from the notebook.
